title: Tenet
events_chronological: As a young man scavenging plutonium in the closed city of Stalsk-12, Andrei Sator finds a buried cache of gold and a message from the future, and is hired to assemble the Algorithm.
In the future, the scientist who built the Algorithm splits it into nine pieces, hides them in the past, and kills herself so that it cannot be rebuilt.
Dying of pancreatic cancer, Sator decides to take the world with him by assembling the Algorithm and reversing entropy.
A CIA operative, the Protagonist, survives a siege at the Kyiv opera house and swallows a cyanide pill that turns out to be a loyalty test, and is recruited into Tenet.
The Protagonist is shown inverted bullets and briefed by the scientist Laura on objects whose entropy runs backwards.
He traces the bullets to the Mumbai arms dealer Priya, who names Sator as the source.
Sir Michael Crosby tells him to reach Sator through his estranged wife Kat, an art appraiser trapped by a forged Goya she authenticated.
The Protagonist and Neil break into the Oslo freeport to steal the forgery and are attacked by a masked man moving backwards through the fight.
Kat introduces the Protagonist to Sator, who tries to have him killed on the yacht.
Sator takes the Protagonist along on a raid to seize plutonium-241 from a motorway convoy in Tallinn.
The Protagonist hides the case, Sator shoots Kat with an inverted bullet, and the Protagonist gives up the case to save her.
The Protagonist and Neil invert themselves and drive the Tallinn chase backwards to recover the case, and the Protagonist fights the masked man in the freeport - himself.
The inverted Kat is taken back through the Oslo turnstile to be healed before the radiation kills her.
The team work out that Sator's dead-man switch will detonate the Algorithm at the moment of his death, on a yacht in Vietnam days earlier.
A temporal pincer movement is mounted at Stalsk-12, with one team moving forward and one backward through the same ten minutes.
On the yacht in Vietnam, Kat keeps Sator alive until the signal comes, and then kills him herself.
In the hypocentre, Ives and the Protagonist reach the Algorithm, and a corpse with a red-tagged rucksack opens the gate for them.
Neil reveals that he was that corpse, that he has known the Protagonist for years from the other direction, and goes back to die.
The Protagonist kills Priya to protect Kat and her son, and understands that he is himself the founder of Tenet who recruited them all.
syuzhet_notes: The film follows the Protagonist's personal timeline, which runs forward, but from told-order bullet 12 that timeline is running backwards through world time - the Tallinn chase and the freeport fight of told-order bullets 6 and 9 are replayed from the other direction, so the audience watches the same events a second time with causes and effects swapped. Told-order bullets 4, 8 and 11 are exposition reaching decades back or centuries forward.
fabula_notes: World chronology and personal chronology diverge for most of the second half, and several characters are present in the same room twice moving in opposite directions, so any single ordering has to pick one clock; this one follows world time. Neil's whole acquaintance with the Protagonist runs opposite to the Protagonist's and is never shown, only stated in his last scene.
